summary: Calibration parsing, production checkpoint identity, and batch provenance are substantially improved, but acceptance is blocked because GUI-generated settings bundles do not capture their source-image list or interactive ROI, and organized-study inputs lose Leica filename identity and consequently fail the required-metadata preflight. The claim that GUI, batch, tuner, and study workflows share reproducible production semantics is therefore not established.

Read-only source inspection and checkpoint hashing completed successfully; no full image stack was run.

findings.title: GUI provenance omits source-image and interactive-ROI identity
findings.impact: GUI preview and GUI batch results cannot be reproduced or independently checked for image order, Z/channel selection, or ROI alignment from their generated settings bundles. This directly contradicts the claim of consistent, provenance-sufficient GUI production semantics.
evidence: sperm_segmentation_saturnv5.7.1.py:11513-11536 records source identity only from cfg['_SOURCE_IMAGE_FILES'].
sperm_segmentation_saturnv5.7.1.py:15479-15530 writes GUI preview provenance without populating _SOURCE_IMAGE_FILES or an ROI_MASK_PATH for the in-memory ROI.
sperm_segmentation_saturnv5.7.1.py:15808-15824 writes GUI batch provenance before constructing the interactive ROI and without populating _SOURCE_IMAGE_FILES.
tests/test_saturn_v571_audit_blockers.py:172-196 does not exercise either GUI path.
findings.recommendation: Before saving any GUI settings bundle, persist the exact applied ROI and exclusion mask, populate the ordered source-image list, and include their hashes, Z indices, channels, shapes, and stack identity. Add focused GUI-path tests asserting nonempty, aligned manifests.

findings.title: Organized study filenames break required Leica metadata resolution
findings.impact: The non-destructive study organizer changes Leica source names to a generic sample_id_z*_ch00 pattern. The production batch runner then cannot discover the Leica XML and fails closed despite the study row retaining the XML path. This breaks a supported study workflow and prevents consistent production semantics.
evidence: sperm_segmentation_saturnv5.7.1.py:11969-11991 creates generic organized filenames and retains calibration_metadata_path separately.
sperm_segmentation_saturnv5.7.1.py:11245-11252 rejects non-Leica filenames when metadata is required.
sperm_segmentation_saturnv5.7.1.py:13353-13386 does not bind calibration_metadata_path to CALIBRATION_METADATA_FILE for explicit application.
production_profiles/saturn_v5_7_1_model_c_epoch003.json:104-105 requires automatic Leica metadata calibration.
findings.recommendation: Apply the row's retained XML explicitly and validate its project/series/source mapping before invoking the batch runner, or preserve Leica source identity in organized filenames. Add an end-to-end focused organizer-to-study-run test with REQUIRE_LEICA_METADATA=true.

limitations: No full image stack was executed, as requested.
Focused pytest execution was unavailable because pytest is not installed in the accessible Python environment.
No other reviewers' outputs were read.
The audit candidate directory is untracked in the worktree, but the reviewed source commit resolved exactly to 8c1f9f53e4a1ab72e66a82ef31b8c675ab9e4bf9.
recommended_follow_up: Remediate both blocking provenance paths and create a superseding audit run.
Add GUI preview and GUI batch provenance tests using an in-memory ROI and ordered multi-Z source list.
Add a focused organized-study test proving retained XML is explicitly matched and applied after filename rewriting.
Run the calibration/provenance tests in the documented project test environment and retain the command output as audit evidence.
